messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide drops price to $0.12 per mile. Wait time now 8 minutes. Coverage expanded to residential areas. Partnership wit
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 79 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.
People around you are stressed: Rick Tanner, Angela Wright. The mood is tense.

Jake closed a 2022 Ram 1500 to a plumbing contractor named Tony DiMaggio on Wednesday afternoon — Tony had come in twice before and walked both times, but Jake ran the RoboRide comparison math on the spot: 28,000 annual miles hauling tools and materials, zero cargo capacity on a robotaxi, $0.12/mile times his actual usage would still leave him stranded on a job site. Tony signed at $34,200 with a $5,500 commission for Jake, the first close in three ticks and the difference between collapse and a month of runway. The Rick Tanner call Thursday went well — Rick said plainly: 'I know what you can do, Jake. You're on my list for the service advisor conversation. Don't take anything else until I call you back, which will be within two weeks.' Not a formal offer but the clearest signal Jake has had. The Maria Santos grant application was submitted online Thursday evening — Jake documented his income loss and dealership employment situation and confirmed eligibility. The honest conversation with his partner happened Friday night after the kids were in bed; she had suspected more than Jake had shared and said she was glad to finally know the full picture. Net savings delta is +$1,388: commission of $5,500 less the monthly deficit of $4,112.
